Every night gets a score out of 100, made of four parts: how long you slept against your goal, how regular your bed and wake times are, how quickly you fell asleep, and how few times you woke. The preset says which of them matters most to you.

Balanced: the length of the night counts most, then regular times, interruptions and falling asleep.
Long sleep: for catching up. Sleeping as long as your goal counts most.
Routine: for a steady schedule. Going to bed and waking at the same times counts most.
Unbroken: for light sleepers. Few and short awakenings count most.

The short tour of how sleep tracking works
Phone on the bed, on charge

Leave the phone on the mattress next to you, screen down and plugged in. Its motion sensor feels when you turn over. On a tablet on a stand, pick \"On a stand\" in the Sleep settings: it listens to the room instead (never recording sound).
The app adds up how much the phone moves every half minute. Quiet stretches are sleep, bigger movements or the screen turning on are being awake. Nothing leaves your phone.
The score has four parts: how long you slept, how regular your times are, how fast you fell asleep and how few times you woke. In the Sleep settings pick what matters most to you.

Each night is drawn across the screen. Orange is awake, so a wake-up in the middle of the night shows. Deep, light and REM are only an estimate from the shape of the night; drag a finger over the chart to read it.

It can start by itself at your bedtime and end when you pick up the phone, and play your Ambience mix that fades out. After a few nights the tab tells you whether the sounds help. Change all of it in the Sleep settings.
